annotations.title: Run a saved Rig for real

description: RUN a rig, for real, right now. Without this an outside agent could AUTHOR a rig,                  schedule it and hang a webhook on it — but never run one on demand, and so never                  test the thing it just built. Name the rig by `rig_id` (one you own or adopted) OR                  by `provider_id` + `external_id` (a published listing — this adopts YOUR OWN copy                  first, then runs it, which also heals a stale adopted copy). `input` is whatever                  the rig's input declares (a token address, a URL, a query). The run bills the                  CALLER's own allowance and executes REAL tools — including money steps if the rig                  has them and you have granted a mandate, so read the rig before running someone                  else's. Returns immediately; results land as TRACES. Every answer carries run_id                  and stage_url: a hosted rokha.ai page showing this run's dashboard to whoever may read                  the run — hand it to your user. wait:true + render:true also returns stage_html (the                  dashboard as one self-contained HTML document, <=200 KB) to render yourself in a                  sandboxed frame (iframe sandbox=allow-scripts, never allow-same-origin); GET                  /api/rigs/runs/<run_id>/stage returns {title, html} later. A PAID rig answers 402                  purchase_required until you hold it: product_get shows the price and any PACK that                  carries it; product_checkout buys it (x402 / usdc / sol, no browser). Requires                  Authorization: Bearer <JWT> or an rk_ key.

input.description: What the run works on. Omit only for input-less rigs.

provider_id.description: With external_id: run a PUBLISHED listing (adopts your own copy first).

render.description: With wait:true: also return stage_html, the run's dashboard as one self-contained HTML document (<=200 KB), to render in a sandboxed frame. stage_url is always returned.

rig_id.description: UUID of a rig you own or adopted.

wait.description: true = hold the call until the run finishes (up to ~5 min) and return its output, steps, status and trace_id in one answer. Default false: returns at once, results land as traces (trace_search by rig_id).
